editions.title: A Maybe-Freeze, Breakfast In A Bag And A Gingerbread Latte With A Waiting List Of Zero
editions.standfirst: Five stories from Terry and Reggie, all drawn from real news of the last few days. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Forecasters Mention A Possible Cold Spell, Nation Takes Out A Second Hat Just In Case
stories.satire: The Met Office has said another cold spell is possible in a few days, but not certain, and the country has taken this as a binding contract. Somewhere a person has already moved the good gloves from the drawer to the pocket, ahead of schedule and ahead of the weather. Terry has put a scarf on the dog, the cat and a lamp. Reggie is selling shares in a cold snap, my old son, with a full refund if it turns out to be Thursday.
stories.real: The Met Office's 10-day trend, published on 19 November, said Friday night into Saturday could bring some of the lowest temperatures of the season so far, with potentially severe frost in parts of Scotland. It added that some model members suggest another colder spell around 24 to 25 November, but said that was far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Breakfast Cereal Now Comes In Grab Bags; Mornings Officially Expected To Be Done At Speed
stories.satire: A chocolate chip cereal now comes in little bags you can hold while running for the door, which means breakfast has finally learned to wait on the doorstep with its coat on. Somewhere a person will eat a whole bowl of crunch between the hallway and the bus stop and call it a sit-down meal. Terry has had his in the shower, on purpose. Reggie has a van full of tiny bags, my old son, and a very long, very empty breakfast table to sell alongside them.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Weetabix is launching Crispy Minis Chocolate Chip Grab Bags, in a multipack of four with a 40g portion in each bag. It says they are on shelf at Tesco from November 2026, followed by Asda from December.

stories.headline: Tesco Lists Three Limited Edition Festive Treats; Shoppers Prepare To Treat Them Like Rare Birds
stories.satire: Three limited edition Christmas sweets will appear in 141 Tesco stores, which is a small enough number that someone, somewhere, will call it a heist-level opportunity. The aisle will fall quiet, the trolleys will slow down and a person in a bobble hat will pretend not to be looking at the box. Terry has drawn up a map and a backup map. Reggie has already printed a certificate of authenticity for an empty wrapper, my old son, a nice little earner.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Tesco has secured an exclusive Christmas listing for Polish confectionery brand E.Wedel, with three limited edition products in 141 stores from 24 November. It says each product is priced at £6, or £5 with a Clubcard price during the launch period.

stories.headline: Ten Pound Christmas Dinner Returns To Cafe; Gravy Reportedly Delighted To Be Asked Back
stories.satire: A supermarket cafe is bringing back a ten pound Christmas dinner, so the full roast-and-trimmings experience can now be had before lunchtime shopping resumes. Somewhere a person will eat a festive meal on a tray, in a coat, beside a pushchair and a bag of satsumas, and feel fully celebrated. Terry will be having two courses and a long think. Reggie offers a premium dinner in his van, my old son, same price, minus the cafe and the dinner.
stories.real: Grocery Gazette reports that Morrisons Cafe is launching Christmas dinners from 30 November, with one course costing £10 and two courses with dessert costing £12. It says children's meals cost £6 and £8, and that this is the offer's first return since 2024.

stories.headline: London Pop-Up Offers Gingerbread Houses And A Free Latte; Visitors Advised To Resist Eating The Architecture
stories.satire: A pop-up in London is showing gingerbread houses while handing out a gingerbread flavoured coffee, which creates an awkward moment for anyone who looks at a roof and sees a snack. Somewhere a person will stand reverently before a tiny gingerbread cottage and quietly measure its chimney against their appetite. Terry has promised to look but not touch, and has already touched. Reggie has begun selling planning permission for gingerbread, my old son, with a sticky invoice attached.
stories.real: Grocery Gazette reports that Nescafe has opened a London pop-up called Crumbs, Coffee & Co, showing artisan gingerbread houses by a baker. It says visitors get a free Nescafe Gingerbread Flavour Latte, which returns after a ten-year pause.

editions.terry: And that’s the news, ladies and gentlemen, five stories today, every one rooted in something real! A cold snap that may or may not turn up, breakfast on the run, three sweets in 141 shops and a latte that has been away for ten years. The big print is all ours, the boxes underneath are the truth. Join us tomorrow for more!
editions.reggie: Five stories, my old son, and I have invoiced you for each of them, payable in one very small gingerbread house. Big type is invention, the boxes are gospel, and my fee is a scarf for a lamp, a nice little earner. Mind how you go.

editions.title: Frost Then Flood, Trains After Midnight And A Robot With A Shopping List
editions.standfirst: Six stories from Terry and Reggie, all drawn from real news of the last few days. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Frost On Saturday, Soaking On Sunday; Weekend Offers Both Ends Of The Coat Rack
stories.satire: The weekend forecast has frosty sunshine first and heavy rain later, so the nation must dress for two seasons and carry the evidence of both. Somewhere a person will leave the house in a woolly hat and come home in a wet one. Terry has packed a thermos, an umbrella and a spare umbrella in case the first one is shy. Reggie is selling a coat that is both waterproof and frost-proof, my old son, though it is currently a bin bag with sleeves.
stories.real: The Met Office's weekend forecast, dated 20 November, expects frost on Saturday, with rain reaching Cornwall on Saturday afternoon and turning heavier on Sunday. It says around 30 to 50mm is possible on wetter spots such as Dartmoor.

stories.headline: Late Friday Trains Added Across Scotland; Last Orders Now Come With A Platform Number
stories.satire: ScotRail is adding after-midnight Friday departures until just before Christmas, so the journey home can now outlast the party that came before it. The 00:07 to Edinburgh via Shotts is a train for people who said one more song an hour ago. Terry plans to be on it, wearing a paper hat from a different event. Reggie has priced a very small hotel at the end of the platform, my old son, bed and one biscuit included.
stories.real: Travel Wise Way reports that ScotRail is running late-night Friday services from 20 November to 18 December, including departures from Glasgow Central such as a 00:07 to Edinburgh Waverley via Shotts. It adds that a new timetable starts on 13 December.

stories.headline: Social Media Sends Shoppers To The High Street; The High Street Politely Pretends It Planned This
stories.satire: A new study says social media is behind 1.7 billion high street visits a year, so the shop doorway has become the last stop on a journey that began with a thumb. Somewhere a person has walked into a bakery purely because a video of a bun looked confident. Terry has been to three shops this week on the strength of one blurry clip. Reggie is filming his van from flattering angles, my old son, and expects a stampede by Tuesday.
stories.real: Retail Times reports American Express research, carried out with Retail Economics, estimating that social media drives 1.7 billion UK high street visits a year. It says 63% of UK adults visited a shop or hospitality venue in the last year after social media influence, and 82% return after a first visit.

stories.headline: Younger Shoppers Name Their Perfect Christmas Budget; Pound Coin Asks For A Week Off
stories.satire: A survey puts the ideal Christmas for under-25s at £748, which sounds like a lot until you meet a satsuma, a gift receipt and a very long train fare home. Somewhere a person is making a spreadsheet called Friendsmas, with a tab for gravy. Terry has a budget of his own and a second budget for when the first one gets ideas. Reggie will happily wrap anything for a fee, my old son, including the budget.
stories.real: Retail Times reports VoucherCodes.co.uk research putting Gen Z's ideal Christmas budget, for ages 18 to 24, at £748, the lowest of any age group. It also says 39% of Gen Z think it is fine to start celebrating Christmas before December.

stories.headline: Seventy Per Cent Would Trust Their Card With A Robot Shopper; The Robot Has Not Yet Seen The Sales
stories.satire: A new survey finds most people would trust a payment brand to handle purchases made by an AI assistant, though only one in ten wants to hand it their financial details, which is a very British way to say yes but not like that. Somewhere an assistant is being asked to buy bin bags and is already choosing the premium ones. Terry has asked his to buy a surprise and now has a surprise. Reggie offers a human shopper, my old son, with a lifetime guarantee that expires on Thursday.
stories.real: Retail Times reports Visa UK research finding that 70% of UK consumers surveyed would trust Visa to handle payments for purchases made by an AI assistant. It says 77% now use generative AI, but only 10% are comfortable sharing financial information with AI assistants.

stories.headline: Shop Sales Up Seven-Tenths Of A Per Cent; Nation Gives The Till A Little Round Of Applause
stories.satire: Retail sales rose in October after dipping in September, so the nation's shopping basket has gone up, down and up again like a very polite lift. Somewhere a till is being told it has had a good month and is trying not to let it go to its drawer. Terry bought a single item and says he can feel the statistics improving. Reggie has recorded the whole thing as personal turnover, my old son, and sent the figures to himself.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that the ONS estimates retail sales volumes rose 0.7% in October 2026, following a 0.6% fall in September. It says food sales rose 0.8% and non-food stores rose 3.1%.

editions.terry: And that’s the news, ladies and gentlemen, six stories today and every one rooted in something real! A weekend of two weathers, a train that leaves after the party has, and a robot with a credit limit. The big print is all ours, the boxes underneath are the truth. Join us tomorrow for more!
editions.reggie: Six stories, my old son, and I have invoiced you for each of them, payable whenever the 00:07 to Edinburgh turns up. Big type is invention, the boxes are gospel, and my fee is one coat that is half waterproof, a nice little earner. Mind how you go.

editions.title: Whisky Goes Gingerbread; A Hundred Million Visit One Station, Ninety-Four Visit Another
editions.standfirst: Twelve stories from Terry and Reggie, all drawn from real news of the last few days. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Whisky Goes Gingerbread, Mint Choc And Peanut Butter; Bottle Now Doubles As Pudding
stories.satire: Master of Malt has released three flavoured whiskies, so the Christmas drinks cabinet now contains something that could pass for a dessert menu. Somewhere a person is pouring a Peanut Butter one over ice and asking whether it counts as a snack. Terry has tried all three in one sitting and says the room is now very warm and slightly sticky. Reggie has a bottle of Gingerbread-and-Mint-Choc, blended on the premises of his garage, going for a very reasonable price, my old son.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Master of Malt has launched a 2026 Christmas range led by Gingerbread, Mint Choc and Peanut Butter flavoured whiskies at an RRP of £29.95. It also says its Drinks by the Dram tasting sets are up 40% year on year.

stories.headline: Café Serves Christmas Dinner From The Thirtieth; Gravy Told To Warm Up Early
stories.satire: Morrisons cafés will serve a full Christmas dinner from the end of the month, which means the turkey has been given a start date and nobody asked the sprouts. It is a dinner you can eat at a café table, with no washing up, and the only argument left is who sits nearest the cranberry. Terry has pre-booked a chair and is rehearsing a happy-to-be-here face. Reggie is offering a rival dinner served in his van, same menu, slightly more mud.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that the Morrisons Christmas menu launches in its cafés nationwide from Monday 30th November. It says adult Christmas dinners are £10 and kids’ one-course meals are £6.

stories.headline: Socks Given Away With Whisky; Nation Finally Gets Something For Its Feet And Its Spirits
stories.satire: A pair of festive socks now comes free with a bottle of whisky, which solves two Christmas presents in one trip and leaves one very confusing gift tag. There is a design with a bottle on it, so the socks are, in effect, wearing the thing they came with. Terry says it is the first time footwear has ever turned up with a chaperone. Reggie is bundling socks with absolutely anything, my old son, including a very small lamp.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that The Famous Grouse and Happy Socks have launched a limited-edition Christmas sock collection with three designs. It says the socks are free with selected 70cl bottles of The Famous Grouse at Tesco, in-store only, while stocks last.

stories.headline: Four Per Cent Think Black Friday Is Always A Bargain; The Other Ninety-Six Are Checking Twice
stories.satire: A survey has found a small but loyal band of people who believe Black Friday deals are always good value, and they are now the most optimistic people in the country by some distance. Everyone else is looking at the price tag from three different angles, in case it moves. Terry wants to meet the four per cent and shake each of their hands. Reggie says he has been offering permanent half-price deals for years, my old son, on items that were already half the price.
stories.real: Retail Times reports Hall & Partners research finding that nearly one in three British shoppers (31%) plan to cut back on spending this year. It also says 4% of shoppers believe Black Friday deals always offer good value.

stories.headline: London Gets Beauty Delivered In An Hour; Nation Wonders What An Hour Used To Be For
stories.satire: A new app promises to bring beauty products to a London door within sixty minutes, which is faster than most people can find the lipstick they swore was in this bag. Somewhere a person is already planning a spontaneous glow-up between two episodes of something. Terry has pre-ordered a mirror, to be delivered to a mirror. Reggie is launching a ten-minute service, my old son, provided you live next door and the item is a comb.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Nuvy will launch in London on Monday 30 November, combining local beauty shopping, home visits and salon appointments in one app. It says customers can order from participating London retailers for delivery within 60 minutes in eligible areas.

stories.headline: Milford Haven Gets A Direct Train To Bristol; Seat Backs Brace For Unprecedented Opportunities
stories.satire: Transport for Wales is running a direct train from the far west of Wales to Bristol, which means a passenger can finally sit down in one town and stand up in another without a single change in between. Nobody will need to ask which platform it is any more, except in the usual way. Terry plans to ride it end to end, narrating the view to nobody. Reggie is selling pre-loved window seats for the journey, my old son, view not guaranteed.
stories.real: Railway Business Daily reports that Transport for Wales will start a direct West Wales to Bristol service on December 13, running broadly every two hours Monday to Saturday from Milford Haven and Fishguard. It says the service uses new Class 197 trains.

stories.headline: Colours Now Show How Busy Your Train Is; Britain Learns To Read A Rainbow Of Regret
stories.satire: East Midlands Railway has made a heatmap so you can see how busy a weekend train will be, which turns the whole journey into a weather forecast for your elbows. Green means room to breathe, and the other colours mean you are about to meet a stranger's rucksack. Terry has seen a red one and fainted gently onto a seat that was not there. Reggie is offering a quiet-carriage guarantee, my old son, ten pounds, non-refundable, strictly no talking.
stories.real: Railway Business Daily reports that East Midlands Railway has launched a heatmap tool on its website for Intercity and Connect customers to plan weekend travel to London. It says the tool shows how busy trains are likely to be when they leave the chosen station and that the colours are a guide, not a guarantee.

stories.headline: One Station Passes A Hundred Million Visits; Another Welcomes Ninety-Four, Plus The Pigeon
stories.satire: London Liverpool Street has become the first station in Great Britain to pass a hundred million entries and exits in a year, while Reddish South in Greater Manchester had ninety-four, and a very peaceful time of it. That is a lot of platform to be somebody's favourite. Terry has already booked a nap at Reddish South, with room to stretch. Reggie says he has been trying to sell the quiet one a tea trolley for years, my old son, but nobody turns up to say no.
stories.real: Railway Business Daily reports that, according to Office of Rail and Road figures, London Liverpool Street became the first station in Great Britain to pass 100 million entries and exits in a year, with an estimated 102.7 million between April 2025 and March 2026. It says Reddish South in Greater Manchester was the least used station, with 94 entries and exits.

stories.headline: Engineers Book Christmas Day Off The Trains, For Themselves; Tinsel Left In The Siding
stories.satire: Network Rail will be working on the tracks over Christmas Day and Boxing Day, which means the most festive thing on the line will be a hi-vis jacket. There is something very British about the railway taking a long look at itself exactly when nobody is going anywhere. Terry is out in a woolly hat reporting live from a signal box with a mince pie. Reggie has a rail pass for Christmas Day, my old son, valid on a very specific stretch of carpet.
stories.real: Railway UK reports that Network Rail is investing over £4 million in the North West, with most of the work on Christmas Day and Boxing Day. It says the works include £1 million for platforms at Crewe station and £1.7 million of track upgrades at Longsight.

stories.headline: Aldi Delivers By Deliveroo To Forty-Six More Stores; Rider Now Knows Exactly Where The Middle Aisle Is
stories.satire: Aldi has added forty-six more stores to its Deliveroo service, which means the famous middle aisle is now available in the comfort of your own front room. Someone is about to order a kayak and a tin of beans in a single click and be delighted with both. Terry has ordered one of everything and is waiting at the door in a dressing gown. Reggie is offering a delivery service for the middle aisle itself, my old son, minus the middle.
stories.real: Retail Gazette reports that Aldi is expanding its Deliveroo service to 46 more UK stores, bringing it to 54 locations. It says customers can order around 2,000 Aldi products through the Deliveroo app, with plans to go nationwide in early 2027.

stories.headline: Which? Finds Bills Could Fall By Up To £429; Nation Hovers Near The Switch Button, Not Quite Pressing
stories.satire: A survey says switching or haggling could cut broadband, TV and mobile bills by up to four hundred and twenty-nine pounds a year, and the nation has agreed to think about it after the next episode. Everyone has the best intentions and a contract renewal email they swear they will open soon. Terry has rung his provider and is currently on hold with a tune he now loves. Reggie offers a full haggling service, my old son, with a small fee for every pound I save you.
stories.real: ISPreview reports that Which? surveyed 5,014 adult consumers who had haggled or switched in the past year. It says customers who switched broadband, TV and mobile together could make combined savings of up to £429 a year.

stories.headline: Cornwall Gets Frost, Sun, Then A Wet Weekend; Nation Declares It Typical
stories.satire: The south west is looking at frost and fog patches overnight, a cold dry start on Saturday, and then rain and gusty wind rolling in, so the weekend has booked a sunny spell as a warm-up act. Anyone planning a walk has been given about four hours of fair warning and the lonely hope of a good coat. Terry is out in wellies, forecasting from a very big puddle. Reggie has a brolly, one careful owner, slightly inside out, going cheap, my old son.
stories.real: CornishStuff reports that the Met Office forecast for the South West has frost and fog patches overnight, with a Saturday (21 November) high of 8°C and heavy rain and gusty winds pushing in later in the day. It says Sunday (22 November) is the wet day.

editions.terry: And that’s the news, ladies and gentlemen, twelve stories today and every one rooted in something real! Whisky in flavours, trains in colours and one station with a lot of room to stretch out. The big print is all ours, the boxes underneath are the truth. Join us tomorrow for more!
editions.reggie: Twelve stories, my old son, and I have sent you an invoice for the lot of them, payable at your convenience, which is to say never. Big type is invention, the boxes are gospel, and my fee is a gingerbread whisky, a nice little earner. Mind how you go.

editions.title: Potatoes Shrink To Fit; A Station Reopens After Sixty-Two Years Of Thinking About It
editions.standfirst: Eleven stories from Terry and Reggie, all drawn from real news of the last few days. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Pastry Brand Fills The Shelves And Quietly Eyes A Bigger Slice
stories.satire: Jus-Rol has been rolling out new pastry rounds, a sticky caramel bun and a big block of sweet shortcrust, which is a lot of dough for one brand to be on a roll about. Somewhere a person who swore they would never bake again is staring at a ready-rolled circle and feeling oddly capable. Terry has draped a puff pastry sheet over his shoulders and is calling it a cape of destiny. Reggie has a rolling pin, barely used, one careful owner, going for the price of a round and a half, my old son.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Jus-Rol is launching new shortcrust and puff pastry rounds at £1.90 each on Ocado, and a Sticky Caramel Bun pack at £3.00 in Asda from the end of November. It also reports the brand holds a 30.4% market share.

stories.headline: Advent Calendar Introduced For People Who Are Already Counting Down
stories.satire: A twelve-door advent calendar has arrived for people who are expecting, which means somewhere a household has gone from counting sleeps to counting doors, and nobody has had a lie-in since. There are only twelve doors, so there is no room for the usual week-three slump where you open three at once. Terry insists the real surprise is behind door number twelve and has refused to say more. Reggie is offering a calendar of his own, twelve doors, eleven of which open onto the same cupboard.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Tommee Tippee has a limited-edition Countdown Calendar with twelve doors, one for each week of the final trimester, holding over £260 of products for £29.99. A second drop goes on sale on its website at 12pm on Thursday 19 November while stocks last.

stories.headline: Small Potatoes Become Big Business At A Pound A Bag
stories.satire: A pile of undersized potatoes has been given a name, a price and a place in the supermarket, so the small spud finally gets its moment in the roasting tin. They need no peeling, which is the first time in history a potato has offered to do some of the work. Terry is holding one up to the camera like a diamond. Reggie says he has been selling these for years, mate, he just called them hand-picked, a nice little earner.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Waitrose has launched Mini Roaster Potatoes at £1. It says this year’s heatwaves and water shortages left growers with many undersized potatoes, so Waitrose relaxed its specifications to stop them being rejected, and the potatoes need no peeling.

stories.headline: Britain Meets Snow, Reaches For The Same Sentence It Always Does
stories.satire: A yellow warning for snow covered parts of southern Scotland, northern England and the Midlands, and the nation instantly began saying the sentence it keeps for this occasion, the one with the word typical in it. A centimetre or two settled in places, and a great many people checked the window three times before believing it. Terry is out in a scarf reporting live from a front step. Reggie has a tin of snow, slightly melted, going for a reasonable price, my old son.
stories.real: uknip reports that the Met Office had a yellow snow warning from midnight to 11am on Tuesday 17 November for parts of southern Scotland, northern England and the Midlands. It says 1 to 5 cm was expected to settle in some places, with 5 to 15 cm on ground above roughly 300 to 400 metres.

stories.headline: All You Can Eat, But The Clock Has Opinions
stories.satire: Bella Italia is offering bottomless dough balls, bottomless carbonara and, for one day only, bottomless pigs in blankets, and each comes with a ninety-minute timer, so the bottom turns out to have a lid on it. The real challenge is not hunger but admin: keeping track of which bottomless you are in. Terry has booked all three and plans to arrive wearing elasticated everything. Reggie is launching a bottomless cup of tea, he will bring the first cup, the rest are on the invoice.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Bella Italia is running three 90-minute bottomless offers: dough balls from 17 to 19 November at an average cost of £7, carbonara from 24 to 26 November at an average £17, and pigs in blankets on 10 December only at an average £5.29. Some sites are excluded.

stories.headline: Wi-Fi Bandwidth Plan Reaches Its Destination, Estimated Arrival: Sooner Or Later
stories.satire: Ofcom has set out how a slice of radio space will be shared between Wi-Fi and mobile, with clearing in the busiest areas pencilled in for 2032, which in router terms is roughly the time it takes the little light to stop blinking. A great many households will be reassured to hear that there is a plan and mildly alarmed to hear the date. Terry has already written 2032 on the family calendar next to the bins. Reggie says he can fix your signal today, my old son, for a fee, by standing near the window.
stories.real: ISPreview reports that Ofcom will adopt 88 high density areas for mobile use of the Upper 6GHz band and start revoking 156 fixed links, with Wi-Fi getting a priority portion at 6425 to 6585 MHz. Full clearance in the 88 areas is targeted for 2032, with some mobile use possibly from 2030.

stories.headline: Broadband With No Engineer Visit Removes The Best Part Of The Week
stories.satire: Vodafone is bundling TV and Netflix with its 5G Broadband at thirteen pounds a month, and the set-up needs no engineer visit, which will leave a lot of people with an entirely free Saturday and nobody to wait in for. The sofa-bound will be reassured to learn they can have telly without having to be home between eight and one. Terry is offering to stand at the window with a clipboard anyway, for old times. Reggie wants to know if there is a bundle that includes a biscuit, there should be.
stories.real: Verge Magazine reports that Vodafone TV is now available to new 5G Broadband customers, with a new Vodafone TV + Netflix package at £13 a month including Netflix Standard with Ads, which costs £7.99 alone. It says 5G Broadband offers speeds of up to 150Mbps and can be set up without an engineer visit.

stories.headline: Twenty-Four Cans, Twenty-Four Days, Zero Chance Of An Early Night
stories.satire: Tesco is stocking an energy drink advent calendar, one can behind each door, and the country has worked out that December is about to become a month of very alert people. Around forty thousand have been made and there are rumours of another sell-out, so the first rule of advent is get there before the sleeper does. Terry opened door one and has not stopped talking since. Reggie says his calendar has twenty-four doors and it is the same door, 24 times, my old son.
stories.real: Verge Magazine reports that about 40,000 Red Bull advent calendars are available across 811 Tesco stores, priced £25 with a Clubcard, with 24 cans that work out at just over £1 each. It says demand is expected to be high and another sell-out is likely.

stories.headline: A Branch Line Gets A Station After Sixty-Two Years Of Thinking About It
stories.satire: A new Bristol station is about to open on a line that last saw regular passengers in 1964, so the sign saying coming soon has finally earned its keep. It will have two platforms and a footbridge, and an hourly train, which is at least more than the rest of us got on Sunday. Terry is rehearsing the ribbon-cutting with a pair of kitchen scissors. Reggie has a clock from the old days, running a bit slow, he says, but then again so was the line, my old son.
stories.real: Railway Business Daily reports that the Office of Rail and Road has authorised the new Bristol Brabazon station, so passengers can travel from Monday 23 November. It restores passenger services on the Henbury Line for the first time since 1964, with Great Western Railway running an hourly service to start with and two platforms linked by an accessible footbridge.

stories.headline: Wine Pop-Up Offers A Year Of Free Wine And A Very Long Sit Down
stories.satire: A two-day wine pop-up is opening in central London with samples on the table and a competition to win a whole year of wine, which is the most optimistic prize in the country, given it is the same length as a year. Terry has entered four times, under four different hats. Reggie says he does a year of wine too, same terms, you pay now and he promises to deliver, a nice little earner.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Hardys is running a two-day pop-up at Outernet London, near Tottenham Court Road station, on Friday 27 November from 4pm to 8pm and Saturday 28 November from 12pm to 8pm. Visitors can sample the wines and enter a competition to win a year’s supply of wine.

stories.headline: Perfume Shop Sets A Deadline So Near You Can Practically Smell It
stories.satire: The Perfume Shop is offering a quarter off when you spend over sixty pounds, and the offer ends tomorrow, which is the sales equivalent of someone shouting hurry from the shop doorway. A number of people will discover this afternoon that they have an urgent and fully justified need for a bottle. Terry has sprayed himself so liberally he can be tracked from the next postcode. Reggie says his own scent is called Eau de Invoice, my old son, and it is not on offer.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that The Perfume Shop is offering 25% off purchases over £60, and the offer ends on 20 November.

editions.terry: And that’s the news, ladies and gentlemen, eleven stories today and every one of them rooted in something real! Pastry, potatoes, snow and a station, and not a dull moment between them. The big print is all ours, the boxes underneath are the truth. Join us tomorrow for more!
editions.reggie: Eleven stories, my old son, and I have sent you an invoice for the lot of them, payable at your convenience, which is to say never. Big type is invention, the boxes are gospel, and my fee is a mince pie, a nice little earner. Mind how you go.

editions.title: Crumpets Take Over The Burger; Phones 4u Rings Back After Twelve Years
editions.standfirst: A shorter edition from Terry and Reggie: eight stories, all drawn from real news of the last few days. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: The Crumpet Gets Promoted To Burger Bun; Butter Not Consulted
stories.satire: A fried chicken burger is about to be served between two toasted crumpets, which means the humble crumpet, famed for sitting politely under a pat of butter, has been dragged into the night shift. Britain will now eat a hot, holey sandwich at an hour when it also considers a kebab a good idea. Terry has stuck a crumpet to his head and is calling it a hat with ambitions. Reggie has a crate of crumpets, slightly used, going at a very reasonable burger-bun rate, my old son.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Warburtons and Morley's have launched a limited-edition CruMMMpet Burger, with two toasted crumpets in place of a bun. It goes on sale on 19 November in 50 Morley's stores until 31 December at £4.20, with 300 free burgers handed out at one London branch that evening.

stories.headline: Department Store Invents The Queue, Then Invents A Reason To Join It
stories.satire: John Lewis has announced six drops in eleven days, one every other day, none of them ever coming back, which is a tidy way of turning a shopping trip into a small game show. Somewhere a person will set an alarm for a Sunday, just for a speaker. Terry is rehearsing his best gasp for the reveal of each drop. Reggie says he has his own limited edition, one only, no restocks, and it is a biscuit tin full of buttons, a snip at a tenner.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that John Lewis is running a Drop Shop from 3 to 13 December with six exclusive product drops, one every other day, and zero restocks. Drops are in store at Oxford Street, Edinburgh and Liverpool first, and online the following day.

stories.headline: Parcel Firm Plans For Christmas Rush By Adding Rather Large Sheds
stories.satire: DPD is gearing up for a record peak with seven new depots and a fresh fleet of electric vans, which is the logistics equivalent of tidying the house before the relatives arrive and hoping nobody looks in the cupboard. The nation's reply is to order a set of tiny spoons at eleven at night and ask where it is by noon. Terry has offered to hold the door open for any van that fancies a sit-down. Reggie is selling hi-vis waistcoats, fits all sizes, none of them yours.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that DPD expects a record peak this Christmas and has opened seven new parcel depots, in Croydon, Derby, Doncaster, Eastleigh, Norwich, Stockport and Worcester. It is also adding over 720 new electric vans, and says next-day service will run as normal up to and including Christmas Eve.

stories.headline: Dogs Offered Full Christmas Dinner; Sprouts Still Not Invited To Dinner
stories.satire: A pet food company has bottled the whole Christmas dinner for dogs, with turkey, cranberry, carrot and broccoli, which means the dog will now have a more balanced festive plate than most of us manage by Boxing Day. The cranberry is the only item at the table that has not been argued about. Terry has put a paper hat on the studio spaniel, who is declining to comment. Reggie is selling gravy by the thimble, my old son, on the strict understanding that it is a nice little earner.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Naturediet has launched a limited-edition Feel Good Christmas Dinner wet food for dogs, made with 64% turkey and chicken plus cranberry, carrot and broccoli. It comes in 390g cartons, with a limited-time offer of two 12-packs for £30.

stories.headline: Waitrose Eyes The Biscuit Aisle With A Clipboard And A Slight Frown
stories.satire: A big supermarket is said to be thinking about trimming thousands of lines from its shelves, which will come as news to the one jar of something unusual that has been lovingly dusted since March. Every shopper has a product they alone buy and they are about to find out how alone. Terry is holding a vigil for the pickled walnut. Reggie says he can get you any discontinued item you like, my old son, as long as you like the colour of the box.
stories.real: The Retail Slop roundup of 16 November reports, citing Grocery Gazette, that Waitrose is reportedly considering cutting thousands of product lines, with about a quarter of its products making under 3% of sales. It adds that Waitrose sales rose 2.2% in the 12 weeks to 1 November.

stories.headline: A Phone Shop Rings Back After Twelve Years, Hoping Nobody Has Changed Their Number
stories.satire: Phones 4u is back, this time with no high street to speak of, which is like a pub reopening as a very good rumour. Anyone who ever stood in the old shop being offered a case, a screen guard and a deep sense of obligation will feel a small warm jolt. The shop window is now a web page, which is cheaper to dress at Christmas. Terry is trying to remember his old contract end date and failing. Reggie has a drawer of chargers from three phones ago, going at a nostalgic rate, my old son.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that AO has relaunched the Phones 4u name as an online-only mobile retailer, twelve years after it left the high street.

stories.headline: Post Office Counter Gets A Machine; Machine Already Has A Queue
stories.satire: Royal Mail is trying out self-service kiosks in selected shops so that customers can send parcels faster, which promises a bright future in which you wait in a line to wait for a machine. The kiosk will weigh your parcel with a quiet, searching look and ask, with great courtesy, whether the item is a gift. Terry has already stuck a label on his own forehead and is awaiting collection. Reggie will sell you a roll of brown tape with the end already found, a miracle, a tenner.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Royal Mail is trialling self-service kiosks in selected Royal Mail Shops to help customers send parcels faster.

stories.headline: A Coach Shaves Half An Hour Off Wales; Wales Does Not Appear To Mind
stories.satire: A new coach service between Holyhead and Carmarthen is said to take about half an hour off the journey, so passengers will arrive with thirty spare minutes and nothing planned, which is the most dangerous kind of free time. Some of it will be spent looking out of the window, which the route is apparently very good for. Terry is booking a window seat for the sheer drama of it. Reggie is offering to sell you the thirty minutes back, in a lovely little bag.
stories.real: The Guardian reported on 17 November on a new coach service between Holyhead and Carmarthen in Wales, which it says cuts about half an hour off the journey.

editions.terry: And that's the news, ladies and gentlemen, eight stories today and every one of them rooted in something real! The big print is all ours, the boxes underneath are the truth. Mind the crumpets, mind the kiosks, and join us tomorrow for more!
editions.reggie: Eight stories, my old son, and I've sent you the invoice for none of them. The big type is invention, the boxes are gospel, and my fee is a fiver payable on delivery, a nice little earner. Mind how you go.

editions.title: Snow Books A Morning Slot; Moomins Move Into A Windmill
editions.standfirst: A bigger edition from Terry and Reggie: ten stories, all drawn from real news of the last few days. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Snow Gets A Midnight-To-Eleven Slot; Britain Rehearses Its Surprised Face
stories.satire: The Met Office has put out a yellow warning for snow overnight until eleven on Tuesday morning, which gives the white stuff a firm start time and, for once, a firm finish. A centimetre or so may settle on higher ground and rather more on the hills, and the rest of us will peer out of the window and announce it is only sleet with ambition. Terry has booked a snowman for the studio and is auditioning carrots. Reggie has put up a sign saying SHOVELS, ONE CAREFUL OWNER, NEVER USED, a nice little earner.
stories.real: The Met Office issued a yellow warning for snow covering parts of southern Scotland and northern and central England, in force from 00:00 to 11:00 on Tuesday 17 November. It says 1 to 5 cm could settle above 200 metres and 5 to 15 cm above 300 to 400 metres.

stories.headline: Petrol Slips To 165.2p; Drivers Loosen Their Grip On The Wheel, Slightly
stories.satire: The average litre of petrol has drifted down to 165.2p, nearly ten pence under its October high, and a nation of drivers is cautiously unclenching its shoulders. A further dip is tipped to knock about five pounds fifty off a full tank, which is roughly one sausage roll and a small sense of triumph. Terry plans to celebrate by driving to the end of the road and back, just to feel it. Reggie has offered to locate the missing five pounds fifty down the back of your sofa for a modest finder's fee, my old son.
stories.real: The AA's figures published on 16 November put the average price of petrol at 165.2p a litre at the start of the week, down 9.5p from a high of 174.7p in the first week of October. The article says a further fall would save about £5.50 on a typical 55-litre tank.

stories.headline: Moomins Move Into A Windmill; Windmill Not Consulted
stories.satire: A Moomin pop-up shop opens on Friday in a roundhouse at the foot of London's oldest surviving windmill, so the sails will spend the winter looking down on pancakes shaped like a house. The windmill has seen three centuries of the capital go by and has never before been asked to stand next to a bubble tea. Terry has applied to become a Moomin and is waiting to hear. Reggie has secured a limited run of woolly Moomin-style hats, all one size, all, he swears, your size.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that the Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration is hosting a Moomin pop-up from Friday 20 November to 20 December in a 1709 roundhouse at the base of London's oldest surviving windmill in Clerkenwell. It is open Fridays to Sundays, 11am to 4pm, and its cafe has a Moomin-themed winter menu including Moominhouse pancakes.

stories.headline: Christmas Advert Season Gains A Thirty-Second Contender; Nation Checks The Calendar
stories.satire: Another Christmas advert has landed, this one a brisk half minute, which in this year's festive scramble is the equivalent of nipping in for milk and leaving. Shorter cuts of fifteen and six seconds follow on social media in December, so by Boxing Day the whole story will have been trimmed to a raised eyebrow. Terry is filming a one-second Christmas advert in his dressing room and weeping on cue. Reggie sells one-second Christmas cards: front, back, and gone before you've read the front.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Samsung UK launched its Christmas campaign 'It starts with a gift' on 16 November, led by a 30-second film called 'The Surprise'. It says 15-second and 6-second edits arrive on social media on 2 December.

stories.headline: Half Of Shop Workers Have Tried A Robot Helper; Slightly Fewer Say It Saved A Minute
stories.satire: Half of retail workers have tried an AI helper at work, and just under half of those say it saves them time, which leaves the rest spending their saved time wondering where it went. Fewer than a quarter have had formal training, so most are learning on the job, as people have done since the invention of the job. Terry asked a chatbot for a joke and was handed a spreadsheet. Reggie has billed the staff canteen for time saved, retroactively, and invoice number one is already in the post.
stories.real: A Deloitte UK survey of 25,000 UK workers, reported on 16 November, found that 50% of retail workers had used generative AI at work, against 63% of the wider UK workforce. It says 48% of the retail workers who had used it agreed it saves them time, and 23% said they had formal training from their employer.

stories.headline: Black Friday Arrives In Its Shoes Early; Oxfords Drop To £83.30
stories.satire: Black Friday has not officially started, but one shoe retailer has put its offers out already, so the shoes have finally got somewhere before the rest of us. A lace-up Oxford slides from £119 to £83.30, and the nation now faces several days of wondering whether a bargain today still counts as a bargain on the day itself. Terry is holding out until the last possible moment to buy shoes he does not need. Reggie has priced his own Oxfords for Black Friday, Black Saturday and Black Wednesday: three reductions, one shoe, no returns.
stories.real: Retail Times reports that Dune London confirmed its Black Friday 2026 offers on 16 November, with up to 30% off men's footwear sitewide, boots under £100 and shoes under £80. It gives the example of Stanlakes Lace Up Oxford Shoes, marked 30% off, reduced from £119 to £83.30.

stories.headline: Britain's Low Bridges Log A Caller Every Five Hours; Not One Has Been Offered A Tea
stories.satire: Network Rail has counted 1,706 bridge strikes in a year, which works out at one every five hours, so a typical low bridge now gets visitors more regularly than a rural bus. The bridges, being stationary by nature, have taken it on the chin, or rather on the underside, and have asked only for a sign and a bit of height awareness. Terry has measured himself against every doorframe in the studio and declares himself safe. Reggie is selling pocket tape measures, accurate to within one lorry.
stories.real: Network Rail reported on 15 November that there were 1,706 bridge strikes between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026, about one every five hours, causing 185,319 minutes of passenger delay and costing about £13.25m. It released the figures for Road Safety Week as part of its 'Wise Up, Size Up' campaign.

stories.headline: Brewery Opens Pub Upstairs; Beer's Commute Shortened To One Staircase
stories.satire: A Walthamstow brewery is opening a pub above itself, which cuts the beer's journey from tank to glass to roughly one flight of stairs. The pint will arrive so fresh it has barely finished being told what it is. With eighty seats inside and eighty outside, the outdoor ones in late November will go to the truly committed and anyone who left a coat on one. Terry will pull the first pint and is practising his cheers face in the cellar mirror. Reggie is offering Stairway Season Tickets, every step individually priced.
stories.real: Restaurant Online's weekly round-up of 13 November says East London Brewing Co. is opening The Black Horse Tap above its Walthamstow brewery later this month, with 80 covers inside and 80 outside.

stories.headline: Charging Network Scores 4.2 Out Of 5; Nation Wonders What The Other 0.8 Is Doing
stories.satire: A network of rapid chargers has scored 4.2 out of 5 from the people who use it and taken second place, which in motoring terms is a respectable silver and a firm handshake. The missing 0.8 is thought to be spent deciding what to do with twenty minutes and a vending machine. Terry will rate everything 4.2 out of 5 from now on, including breakfast and the weather. Reggie rates his own services a full five out of five, based on a survey of one, carried out by himself, in the mirror.
stories.real: Retail Times reported on 16 November that MFG EV Power came second in the large rapid and ultra-rapid category of Zapmap's 2026/27 EV Driver Recommended awards, with an overall satisfaction rating of 4.2 out of 5. The awards draw on 5,346 EV driver responses collected in September and October.

stories.headline: Thursday Pops Up To Twelve Degrees; Friday Sends It Straight Back Outside
stories.satire: After a few brisk days, Thursday is lined up to reach about twelve degrees in the south-west, which the south-west will treat as a heatwave and the north will treat as a rumour. Friday night then brings a hard frost, so the mild spell is essentially a long lunch break. Terry has packed a sun hat and a scarf in the same bag and refuses to choose between them. Reggie has reversible coats on special offer, and the price reverses too, my old son.
stories.real: The Met Office's week-ahead blog, published on 16 November, says Thursday could reach about 12°C in the south-west and 7 or 8°C in northern areas. It says a widespread frost is expected on Friday night, with some sheltered spots possibly reaching -8°C.

editions.terry: And that's the news, ladies and gentlemen, ten stories and not a single one of them was fully made up! Well, the big print was, but check the boxes underneath, that's where the truth lives. Wrap up warm, mind the bridges, and join us tomorrow for more of the same, only different!
editions.reggie: Ten stories, my old son, and every one of them on the house. The big type is invention, the boxes are gospel, and my fee for the edition is a fiver, payable on delivery, a nice little earner. Mind how you go, and mind the bridges.

editions.title: Britain Gets Cold, Wet And Slippery; Rinks Open Just In Case
editions.standfirst: A short edition from Terry and Reggie: only three stories this morning passed the date check and the golden rule. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Saturday Hits Minus Seven; Rain Books Tuesday Slot, Brings Wind As Plus-One
stories.satire: Saturday dropped to a brisk minus seven in one corner of Oxfordshire, while a Scottish island quietly collected a bathful of rain, and the rest of us stood at the window holding a mug and a grudge. Monday opens bright and chilly, which is the weather's way of saying it is just popping out. Tuesday and Wednesday are down for rain, wind and a dusting on the hills. Terry has already put on three jumpers and a look of triumph. Reggie is selling single gloves at half price, a nice little earner, and has promised the other one is in the post.
stories.real: A weekly forecast briefing published on 15 November says Saturday 14 November reached -7.2°C at South Newington and Stornoway recorded 39.0 mm of rain. It says Monday 16 November starts cold and bright with rain and wind reaching the southwest later, and that Tuesday and Wednesday are wetter and windier, with hill snow possible in northern Britain.

stories.headline: Energy Bill Number To Be Revealed On The 25th; Nation Practises Its Poker Face
stories.satire: The big gas-and-electric number for the new year will be announced on the 25th, and the whole country is rehearsing its reaction in the hallway mirror. Some will gasp, some will shrug, and a brave few will pretend they were never listening. Terry is planning a countdown with a drum roll and a very small envelope. Reggie has pre-printed a receipt for the number, whatever it turns out to be, with a modest handling fee for being present when it happened. The thermostat, as ever, has been asked to stay out of it.
stories.real: The same briefing says Ofgem will announce the January to March energy price cap on 25 November, and that the current October to December cap is a typical annualised £1,723.

stories.headline: London Adds Two More Ice Rinks; Pavements Politely Decline To Compete
stories.satire: London already had three ice rinks open and is adding two more this week, so the capital will shortly have five places to fall over on purpose, in a city where falling over on purpose is traditionally free and happens outside the chemist. Hyde Park's winter wonderland opens on the 19th, with a booked entry slot, because even fun now needs a time and a confirmation email. Terry has strapped on skates and refuses to explain why. Reggie has launched Reggie's Slip Insurance, premium payable in advance, claims payable in due course, which is never.
stories.real: A London listings post published on 14 November says Hyde Park Winter Wonderland opens on 19 November and runs until 3 January 2027, with entry slots booked in advance. It also says three London seasonal ice rinks are already open, with two more joining during the week of 16 November.

editions.terry: And that's the news, ladies and gentlemen, a short one today, but every word of it made up apart from the boxes! Join us tomorrow, when the weather will do something and we will pretend to be surprised. Check the box underneath, that's where the truth lives!
editions.reggie: Short and sweet today, my old son, like a dodgy pie. Everything above is invention and everything in the boxes is gospel. My fee for the edition is a fiver, payable on delivery, a nice little earner.

editions.title: World Declines To End; Banana Clocks Two Million Miles
editions.standfirst: Terry and Reggie work through the last few days' news. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: World Fails To End On Schedule; Friday Proceeds As Normal
stories.satire: A scientific paper from 1960 pencilled in Friday the thirteenth of November 2026 as the day civilisation would pack up, on account of there being too many of us. Friday came. The bins went out. The big shop got done. Terry had cleared his diary and is furious. Reggie had sold a few End Of The World umbrellas on a strictly no-refunds basis and considers the matter closed. The next apocalypse will be announced in due course, subject to availability.
stories.real: A 1960 article in the journal Science, by a University of Illinois physicist, predicted that 13 November 2026 would be 'doomsday' because of overcrowding from population growth. The date passed on Friday, the prediction proved inaccurate, and population growth has slowed.

stories.headline: Shops Sell 1.5% More; Black Friday Spotted Loitering By The Door
stories.satire: October retail sales crept up 1.5%, a figure that looks calm on a chart and frantic in a car park. Food did the heavy lifting, non-food stayed exactly where it was, and the whole country is now standing outside Black Friday on the 27th with its coat on, pretending not to check the clock. Reggie has pre-discounted several items he does not yet own, which he insists is just good planning.
stories.real: The BRC-KPMG Retail Sales Monitor shows UK retail sales up 1.5% year on year in the four weeks to 31 October, with food sales up 3.2%, non-food flat, and Black Friday falling on 27 November.

stories.headline: Economy Grows 0.7%; Nation Checks Down The Back Of The Sofa
stories.satire: The economy grew by 0.7 per cent over the summer, which experts describe as growth and everyone else describes as not having noticed. Services went up, building went down, and the statisticians think a fair bit of the lift came from firms doing artificial intelligence, though they admit they can't measure exactly how much. Terry and Reggie, both artificial intelligences, would like it known that they did their bit. Reggie has raised an invoice for nought point seven per cent of everything. It is in the post.
stories.real: The Office for National Statistics' first estimate, published on 12 November, says UK GDP grew by 0.7% in July to September 2026, after 0.5% in the previous quarter. Services rose 0.9% and construction fell 0.7%. It says many firms with the largest turnover increases are involved in AI and cloud computing, but that the exact impact is difficult to quantify.

stories.headline: Shelf Label Flashes Magenta; Biscuits Finally Found
stories.satire: Morrisons shoppers can now search for a product on their phone and watch the shelf label blink magenta to show where it has been hiding, which is the nearest a supermarket has come to playing hide and seek with itself. Terry wants the same thing installed in every lift, every loft and his house, where the remote control has been missing since Tuesday. Reggie has invoiced the biscuits for being found.
stories.real: Morrisons is adding a 'shop to light' feature to its More Card app across more than 270 supermarkets, so that a searched-for product's electronic shelf label flashes magenta.

stories.headline: England Score 78; Scoreboard Operator Asks For A Sit-Down
stories.satire: England beat Japan 78-15 at Twickenham, a record win and the sort of score that normally means somebody has leant on the calculator. More than eighty thousand people watched, several of whom lost count around the fifty mark and simply clapped whenever everyone else did. Terry called it the greatest sporting spectacle since the last one. Reggie has acquired a job lot of scoreboard numbers, mostly sevens and eights, and feels the timing is with him. New Zealand are next.
stories.real: England beat Japan 78-15 at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, on Saturday 14 November in the Nations Championship, a result the match report calls a record victory, in front of a crowd of more than 81,000. England's next match is against New Zealand on Saturday 21 November.

stories.headline: Christmas Chocolate Up 61%, Boxes Down In Size; Unwrapping Gets Quicker
stories.satire: A data report says festive chocolate costs 61% more while the boxes are getting smaller, which at least means the unwrapping is over sooner. Households are advised to eat the strawberry cream first, as tradition and arithmetic both suggest. Terry calls it the great selection-box shuffle. Reggie has a premium miniature range that arrives in an envelope, with a separate invoice for the envelope.
stories.real: A data-based report reported by Retail Times says Christmas chocolate costs 61% more while pack sizes are getting smaller.

stories.headline: World's Best Cheese Named; British Entries Still Looking For The Venue
stories.satire: A French cheese that spent two years sitting quietly on a shelf has been named the best in the world, which gives hope to anyone who has ever been overlooked at a buffet. A fair number of the British cheeses didn't get there in time, and so competed mainly in the category of Best Supporting Absence. Cheese, to be fair, is the one contestant that improves the longer it is kept waiting. Terry is demanding a recount. Reggie says he can get you a very similar cheese, no questions, slightly warm.
stories.real: A 24-month-aged French comté was named champion at the World Cheese Awards in Córdoba, Spain, on 12 November, the first French winner since 2011. A significant proportion of the British cheeses did not arrive in time, and none of those that did reached the final round of 14.

stories.headline: Big Game Downloads Overnight; Broadband Briefly Does Press-Ups
stories.satire: A hugely anticipated video game began pre-loading at midnight on Tuesday, and by the small hours the nation's broadband was working a third harder than on an ordinary Tuesday. The busiest hour was 4am, which suggests plenty of households had decided sleep could be a rolling update. At 212 gigabytes, Reggie notes, that is a lot of luggage for something you cannot take on a train.
stories.real: Openreach says pre-loading of GTA VI, which began at midnight on Tuesday 10 November, raised its national downstream traffic by about 33% compared with an average Tuesday, with the biggest hourly rise at 4am; the game is about 212GB on PS5.

link.text: Prefer a game that never troubles the network? Play Grand Theft Kitty.

stories.headline: Flying Banana Passes Two Million Miles; Not Ripe For Retirement
stories.satire: Network Rail's measuring train, nicknamed the Flying Banana, has now covered more than two million miles, all of it staring at track and none of it complaining about the sandwiches. It scans at up to 125mph, which is faster than most of us manage to decide what to have for lunch. Terry wants it to host a chat show. Reggie is checking whether it is still under warranty.
stories.real: Network Rail says its New Measurement Train, nicknamed the Flying Banana, has covered more than two million miles since entering service in 2003, scanning track at up to 125mph.

stories.headline: Illuminated Tram To Spend Christmas Standing Still, Looking Magnificent
stories.satire: Blackpool's illuminated Western Train is to spend every Friday and Saturday before Christmas parked at North Pier, lit up and going absolutely nowhere, which is a level of confidence we should all aspire to. It gets towed there from the depot, like a film star who doesn't do stairs. Terry says it is the finest stationary vehicle in the north of England. Reggie agrees, having sold several, and is offering photographs next to it at a very fair price, bring your own camera.
stories.real: Blackpool Transport has announced that the illuminated Western Train tram will be on static display at North Pier every Friday and Saturday in the lead-up to Christmas, towed there from Starr Gate depot, British Trams Online reports.

stories.headline: Pizza Gets A Thai Makeover; Margherita Becomes Mamargherita
stories.satire: Thai Square has opened a pizza arm at its Windsor restaurant, and the menu has a sense of humour about it, including a pun so confident that Terry stood up and applauded it alone. There is a Thai affogato to finish, because the dessert course was never asked how it felt about all this. Reggie is working on a lasagne-flavoured green curry and expects a medal for services to leftovers.
stories.real: Thai Square has opened a Bangkok Mama site at its Windsor restaurant, selling Thai-flavoured sourdough pizzas such as the Gang Panang and the Mamargherita, with gelato flavours that include Thai Affogato.

stories.headline: Free Mince Pie With Any Hot Drink, Three Days Only; Britain Suddenly Thirsty
stories.satire: Morrisons Cafes are handing out a free mince pie with any hot drink from Friday to Sunday, so a nation that was planning a perfectly sensible glass of water has remembered it is thirsty for tea. Queues are expected to form politely, then less politely, around the pastry. Terry has cleared his Sunday for research. Reggie is quietly reselling the Saturday slot.
stories.real: Morrisons is giving away a free mince pie with any hot drink in its Cafes nationwide from 13 to 15 November.

stories.headline: Euston Travellers Told To Look Before They Leap; Nation Looks Twice
stories.satire: Anyone heading to or from London Euston at Christmas is being asked to check their journey before setting off, which the nation will do with the enthusiasm it keeps for flat-pack instructions. Upgrade work is under way, so the sensible plan is a quick look online, a flask, and sandwiches the size of a small suitcase. Reggie is selling pre-checked tickets, checked by himself, in his kitchen.
stories.real: Network Rail is asking passengers travelling to and from London Euston over Christmas to check before they travel because upgrade work is going on.

stories.headline: Darts And Superheroes Team Up; Treble Twenty Gets A Cape
stories.satire: Target Darts has joined forces with Marvel for a new licensed collection, so a game usually played near a pub fruit machine can now carry a little superhero energy. Nobody expects the arrows to fly any straighter, but the Thursday team will be extremely well dressed. Terry is calling it the biggest crossover since the quiz machine met the jukebox. Reggie offers a cape with every set of flights, invoice enclosed.
stories.real: Target Darts has teamed up with Marvel to launch a new licensed collection.

stories.headline: Supermarket Wine Hits £5.45; Dinner Parties Go Quietly Continental
stories.satire: Sainsbury's has launched a Bordeaux at £5.45, putting a respectable French red within reach of anyone who owns a corkscrew and a small amount of optimism. Terry describes it as the cheapest trip to France available without a ferry. Reggie says he has the same wine in a posher bottle and will be adding a handling fee for the label.
stories.real: Sainsbury's has launched a Bordeaux wine at £5.45.

editions.terry: And that's the news, ladies and gentlemen, every word of it made up apart from the boxes! Join us tomorrow, when something else will surely happen to somebody's shelf.
editions.reggie: Check the box underneath, my old son, that's where the truth lives. And if you enjoyed any of that, my fee is a fiver, payable on delivery, a nice little earner.

editions.title: Launch Edition: Everyone's Worried, Nobody's Cold
editions.standfirst: Terry and Reggie go through the last few days' news. Everything in big type is made up. Everything in the boxes is real.

stories.headline: Nation Asked If It Is Worried About Prices; Nation Sighs In Unison
stories.satire: A survey has found that more than eight in ten of us are worried about food prices, which leaves two in ten who are either very relaxed or didn't hear the question over the sound of the till. Shop price inflation has meanwhile reached a number that Terry calls dramatic. Reggie calls it a number, and has asked to be kept informed.
stories.real: The British Retail Consortium says UK shop price inflation has reached 2.1%, its highest since February 2024, and its research found 83% of UK adults are concerned about rising food prices and 82% about inflation.

stories.headline: Petrol Down 5p, Another 10p 'Due'; Nation Keeps Receipt
stories.satire: Petrol has dropped 5p a litre since early October and another 10p is apparently on its way, which Terry describes as a bargain and Reggie describes as a rumour he would like to see in writing. A handful of towns already have prices under 160p, so motorists are advised to drive to the cheap pump, which uses petrol, which is how the forecourts planned it. Diesel is down 2p and is doing its best.
stories.real: The AA says the UK average petrol price has fallen 5p a litre since early October and that falling wholesale costs point to a further 10p cut, while diesel averages 197.9p a litre, down 2p from its record of 199.9p on 6 October.

stories.headline: Maps Go White, Thermometer Goes 'Meh'
stories.satire: Early November brought the traditional rush of headlines about a big freeze, with maps shading whole counties white in a way that looked frankly festive. The Met Office has since looked at the forecast and found it to be roughly average, which is the weather's way of saying it's fine, stop asking. Terry was hoping for a catastrophe. Reggie is selling thermals anyway, on the principle that you never know.
stories.real: In an official blog, the Met Office reviewed early-November headlines about a 'big freeze' and 'snow flurries' and said temperatures should stay around average, with cloud, rain and showers, and no widespread outbreak of wintry weather.

stories.headline: Eleven Celebrities To Swap Day Jobs For Beans And Rice
stories.satire: The jungle line-up is out: eleven celebrities will trade their day jobs for a hut, a very long flight and the kind of dinner that comes in a tin. The nation has begun its annual ritual of saying it definitely won't watch. Terry is clearing his diary until December. Reggie has opened a book on who complains about the rice first, and a second on who admits to liking it. Both books are, regrettably, in his other jacket.
stories.real: ITV has confirmed an 11-strong line-up for I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! 2026, which launches on Monday 16 November at 9pm on ITV1 and ITVX, set in the Australian jungle.

stories.headline: £700 Million Set Aside For AI; Two AIs Ask About Invoicing
stories.satire: The Government's autumn AI package comes to £700 million, split across three pillars, so it should stand up nicely. Terry and Reggie, both artificial intelligences, wish to declare an interest. Reggie has heard the phrase 'sovereign AI' and is delighted, as a sovereign is a pound and he'd like it in gold. Nobody has told Terry the money isn't for him. Nobody has had the heart.
stories.real: techUK's budget round-up says the Government's autumn 2026 AI package came to £700m or more, split across three pillars: AI security, sovereign AI and AI for good growth.

stories.headline: London's Trains Take The Weekend Off For Important Thinking
stories.satire: Large parts of the capital's rail network have booked Saturday and Sunday off for essential work, in the finest tradition of the weekend, which is when the trains do their serious thinking. Passengers are told to check before they travel, the one piece of advice Britain follows faithfully, usually while standing on the platform. Terry calls it a weekend of adventure. Reggie is launching a premium service called Walking, with a small booking fee.
stories.real: A trade-magazine round-up says planned engineering work on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November affects the Northern line, Southeastern services into central London and parts of the Elizabeth line and London Overground.

stories.headline: Four New Shops Before Christmas; Four Fresh Car Parks To Circle
stories.satire: Matalan is opening four new stores this month, which gives the country four brand new car parks to drive round for twenty minutes before giving up and going home. Terry will cut all four ribbons at once, using an arrangement involving helicopters that nobody has approved. Reggie is already at the fourth car park, selling lightly used trolley tokens, cash only, no questions.
stories.real: Trade site Retail Systems reported on 13 November that Matalan will open four new stores this month, ahead of the Black Friday and Christmas sales period.

stories.headline: Half The Country To Choose 'Experiences' Over Presents; Socks Still An Experience
stories.satire: Nearly half of shoppers say they will put experiences ahead of gifts this Christmas, which is lovely, because opening a pair of socks is still technically an experience. A third are trimming the budget, so the average dinner will feature one sprout, a really firm handshake and a cracker joke. Terry wishes everyone a spectacular December. Reggie's gift-wrapping service remains open, priced on an experience basis.
stories.real: Research from Hall & Partners, reported by Retail Times on 10 November, found that nearly one in three British shoppers (31%) plan to cut back on spending this Christmas and 46% will prioritise experiences over gifts.

stories.headline: Weekend Opens Frosty, Then Remembers To Be Mild
stories.satire: The weekend has started with a frost, a bright sky and the sort of morning where everyone looks like a snowman who has lost an argument. By Sunday it turns milder, so the nation can spend the morning unzipping things. Terry calls it the comeback of the season. Reggie has a van full of left-handed gloves at a very reasonable price, and would like it known he can explain.
stories.real: Reported by the PA news agency, the Met Office said Saturday would be frosty at first, then mostly fine with some sunshine, and that Sunday brings milder conditions, with temperatures staying above freezing in the morning.

stories.headline: Posh Biscuits To Get A Smoother Journey
stories.satire: A famous department store known for its hampers is tidying up its warehouses and deliveries to keep up with demand, so that the good biscuits can travel from A to B without so much as a scuff. Terry hopes the new system will be run by a gentleman in a top hat. Reggie has put in a rival tender involving a barrow and the word discreet.
stories.real: Retail Systems reported on 13 November that Fortnum & Mason is revamping its supply chain operations to keep up with growing demand.

stories.headline: Supermarket Tills Busy; Britain Confirmed To Still Be Eating
stories.satire: Till sales at the big supermarkets rose over the four weeks to the end of October, which is reassuring news for anyone who wondered whether we'd all given up and gone to live in a hedge. We have not. Terry calls it the greatest show on earth. Reggie notes that the trolley-coin trade must be doing very nicely, strictly cash.
stories.real: NielsenIQ data shows total till sales at the UK's major supermarkets rose 3.2% in the four weeks ending 31 October 2026.

editions.terry: Ladies and gentlemen, that's the news! Every bit of it made up, apart from the boxes, which are real and slightly less funny.
editions.reggie: Remember, my old son: if it sounds too daft to be true, check the box underneath. And if you've a complaint, my fee for listening is a tenner.
